claims.text: A combined route of SLM using low-oxygen gas-atomized powder, followed by SPS and HPT, will produce a nanocrystalline single-phase BCC Group IV–V RHEA.
The feedstock can be a gas-atomized Group IV–V RHEA powder with oxygen content below 0.02 at.%.
SLM of NbMoTaW at a linear energy density of at least 2.83 J/mm can form a single BCC solid solution.
The high cooling rate of SLM suppresses brittle intermetallic nucleation and promotes a single BCC solid solution.
SPS after SLM will ensure full density without significant grain growth.
Gas-atomized low-oxygen HfNbTaTiZr powder can be fully densified by SPS.
SPS followed by HPT refines HfNbTaTiZr to a grain size well below 500 nm.
HPT will introduce a high dislocation density in the processed RHEA.
Residual oxygen or nitrogen will provide interstitial solid-solution strengthening and increased lattice friction.
Interstitial strengthening and high lattice friction will stabilize the nanocrystalline BCC matrix and prevent Laves, silicide, B2, and oxide formation.
Grain refinement will increase yield strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
The combination of grain refinement and interstitial strengthening will enhance both yield strength and ductility, mitigating refractory-alloy brittleness.
The resulting SLM–SPS–HPT material will have room-temperature tensile yield strength above 1400 MPa and elongation above 20%.
The resulting material will have a peak damping capacity of approximately 0.03 near 800 K.
The resulting material will contain no significant brittle Laves or oxide phases.
The proposed microstructure will retain structural integrity during testing at temperatures up to 800–1000 K.
Conventional arc-melted or cast RHEAs typically have coarse microstructures, brittle-phase segregation, high oxygen content, and low ductility.
High concentrations of Al, Cr, or Si can form brittle intermetallics even under rapid cooling.
High initial oxygen content above 2 at.% falls outside the range where the proposed route is expected to mitigate brittleness.

contradictions.description: WVTaTiCr is offered as an example target alloy, while the boundary states that the hypothesis may not hold for systems with high Cr concentrations; a nominal near-equiatomic WVTaTiCr alloy would contain substantial Cr.

Failure of a high-oxygen sample or a sample made without HPT would support the asserted need for low oxygen and HPT, not falsify the performance of the complete proposed route. The high-oxygen sample is also explicitly outside the stated applicability boundary.
